question: Fed rate hike in 2026?
resolution_criteria:
This market will resolve to “Yes” if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate is increased at any point between January 1, 2026 and the Fed's December 2026 meeting, currently scheduled for December 8-9, 2026. Otherwise, this market will resolve to “No”.

This market may not resolve to "No" until the Fed has released its rate change decision following its December meeting.

The primary resolution source for this market will be the official website of the Federal Reserve (https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm), however a consensus of credible reporting may also be used.

- 2026-07-29: Three regional Fed presidents dissented in favor of a 25 bp hike: Hammack (Cleveland), Kashkari (Minneapolis) and Logan (Dallas). [Kiplinger](https://www.kiplinger.com/investing/live/fed-meeting-updates-and-commentary-july-2026), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/29/fed-rate-decision-july-2026.html)

Energy fell 1.5% on the month, but gasoline was still about 25% higher than a year earlier because of the Iran war. Afterward, CME FedWatch put a September hike at 38.1%, and economists said nothing in the report "demands" a September hike. Traders cut September hike odds from 57% to 44%. [babypips](https://www.babypips.com/news/headline-us-nonfarm-payrolls-july-2026-jobs-report-fed-rate-outlook), [Fox Business](https://foxbusiness.com/economy/us-jobs-report-july-2026)
- 2026-07-13 to 07-23: Hike odds rose with oil prices after Trump reinstated the blockade of Iranian ports near Hormuz. FedWatch put a July hike at about 36-38%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/23/fed-interest-rate-odds-oil-jobless-claims.html), [Forbes](https://www.forbes.com/sites/simonmoore/2026/07/23/markets-see-chance-fed-hikes-next-week-at-july-meeting/)
- Trump keeps calling for lower rates while defending Warsh, whom he appointed. [ADN/AP](https://www.adn.com/nation-world/2026/08/28/fed-chair-warsh-signals-rate-hikes-may-be-needed-with-inflation-stubbornly-elevated/)

## 4. Base rates
- The last Fed hike was in 2023. Since then the Fed has either cut or held, and the range had come down to 3.50%-3.75% by 2026.
- Historically, it is rare for the Fed to start hiking within about a year of its last cut. One Yahoo headline said traders gave Warsh a 42% chance of doing something that "has only happened once in the past 36 years". I could not open the article to confirm what that refers to or when it was published. [Yahoo](https://finance.yahoo.com/economy/policy/articles/traders-warsh-42-chance-doing-082651946.html)
- In the July meeting, a 9-3 vote with three dissents for a hike is an unusually hawkish split.

# Fed rate hike in 2026: research brief (information as of 2026-08-29)

## 1. Resolution source
- The fetch of the Fed's [open market page](https://www.federalreserve.gov/monetarypolicy/openmarket.htm) failed ("proxy refused the connection"), so I could not read it directly.
- 2026-07-29: The FOMC kept the target range at **3.50% to 3.75%** by a 9-3 vote. Hammack, Kashkari and Logan dissented because they wanted a 25 bp hike. Interest on reserve balances stayed at 3.65%. [Fed press release](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm)
- The rate was 3.50% to 3.75% at the end of 2025 as well. This is background knowledge I did not confirm on the page. It means the upper bound had not risen at any 2026 meeting through July.

## 2. Current status
- 2026-06-17: In the June projections, the median 2026 dot moved up to about 3.75-3.8%, which implies one quarter-point hike this year. Reportedly 9 of 18 participants projected a hike. Chair Warsh did not submit a dot. [investinglive](https://investinglive.com/central-banks/fed-dot-plot-signals-another-2026-rate-hike-as-growth-strengthens-and-inflation-remains-elevated/), [stockhub](https://stockhub.kr/en/insights/979707f3-2dde-44e5-b006-bbd7b1f84281)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-08-28: At Jackson Hole, Chair Warsh said progress on inflation is not enough and that the Fed "has more work to do," and said hikes are possible. He gave no timeline and said his remarks were not forward guidance. [Al Jazeera](https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/8/28/us-fed-chair-warns-inflation-progress-insufficient-hints-at-rate-hikes), [Axios](https://www.axios.com/2026/08/28/kevin-warsh-federal-reserve-jackson-hole), [PBS](https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/warsh-raises-stakes-for-feds-next-meeting-and-other-takeaways-from-jackson-hole-conference)
- 2026-08-28: After the speech, the 2-year Treasury yield rose to about 4.31%. CME FedWatch put the chance of a September hike at about 56%. Economist Heather Long expects any hike to come in October or December rather than September. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/kevin-warsh-jackson-hole-federal-reserve-inflation.html), [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/28/-september-fed-decision-now-a-coin-flip-as-rate-hike-odds-increase.html)
- 2026-08 (late): Fox Business reports July PCE inflation at 3.7% year over year. Another source reports core PCE up 0.2% month over month. [Fox Business](https://www.foxbusiness.com/economy/what-warshs-jackson-hole-speech-signals-about-where-interest-rates-headed), [cryptobriefing](https://cryptobriefing.com/us-core-pce-rises-02-in-july-consumer-spending-stalls/)
- 2026-08-12: July CPI rose 0.1% for the month and 3.4% from a year earlier. Energy was up about 14.7% year over year. Reported core figures conflict across sources, so check bls.gov. After the report, odds of a September hike reportedly fell to about 40%. [Babypips](https://www.babypips.com/news/headline-us-cpi-july-2026-results-fed-rate-decision-2026-08-12)
- 2026-08-07: The July jobs report came in well below expectations. Kalshi put a September hold at 65% and FedWatch put it at about 60%. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/08/07/odds-the-fed-hikes-in-september-tumble-following-big-july-jobs-miss.html)
- 2026-07-29: The July statement cited inflation that is "elevated... in part reflecting supply shocks" and uncertainty from the Middle East conflict. [Fed](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260729a.htm)

## 4. Base rates
- Through the end of August, 5 of the 8 scheduled 2026 meetings have passed, all without a hike. Three remain.
- In recent cycles, the Fed turned from cutting to hiking within about a year only rarely, and usually because inflation was high, as in 2022. Three hawkish dissents and a June median implying a hike are typical signs before a turn like that. This is a qualitative assessment; I did not find a sourced statistic.
- The last FOMC hike was in July 2023, and the Fed cut rates from late 2024 through 2025. This is background knowledge.

## 5. Other forecasts
- 2026-08-29: Polymarket's September-meeting hike market was about 49.5%, up from a cycle low of about 24.5% around Aug 15-17. Kalshi's September hike contract was about 51 cents after Jackson Hole, up from 26 cents on Aug 15. These figures come from a third-party tracker. [macroodds](https://macroodds.com/blog/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026), [predictionmarketspicks](https://predictionmarketspicks.com/articles/fed-rate-hike-odds-september-2026-kalshi-polymarket-futures)
- I could not find an August price for Polymarket's market on this exact question, [Fed rate hike in 2026?](https://polymarket.com/event/fed-rate-hike-in-2026). It should be well above the odds for September alone, because October and December also count.
- 2026-08: MUFG's base case is that the Fed holds through 2026. It expects the market's hike odds for each meeting to stay within 30-60%. [MUFG](https://www.mufgresearch.com/rates/august-2026-fed-rates-call-update/)
- Late June: one blog cited CME FedWatch at about 61% for an October hike. That figure is old and second-hand. [noradarealestate](https://www.noradarealestate.com/blog/interest-rate-predictions-for-the-rest-of-2026/)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- About 2026-09-04: August jobs report. The July report's large miss was what pushed the odds down earlier in August.
- About 2026-09-10/11: August CPI and PPI.
- Other things to watch: Fed officials speaking before the pre-meeting blackout, energy prices tied to the Middle East conflict, and the late-September PCE release.

**Caveat:** Every attempt to fetch a page directly failed, so the facts above come from search-result summaries. Several of them are from secondary sites with conflicting numbers, especially for core CPI. Check the key figures against federalreserve.gov and bls.gov.
